definition: One-shot learning is a problem setup in machine learning which leverages a singular example to assist with classification, originating in the field of computer vision to assist with object categorization.
details: Whereas most machine learning classification methods require training on hundreds or thousands of examples, one-shot learning aims to classify objects from one example. Few-shot learning is used for similar methods which utilize more than one example to assist with classification.

explainer.lead: One-shot learning asks a model to classify a new object from a single labelled example. It matters because many real categories have almost no labelled data available.

tiers.eli5: It is like recognising a new animal after seeing one picture of it, instead of needing a whole photo album first.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers handle it with metric or embedding-based models that compare a query image to one reference image. A common pitfall is that accuracy collapses when the single example is atypical or poorly framed.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the learner must generalise from a support set of size one to unseen queries; most methods learn a similarity function rather than class weights. Limits: results are fragile with one example, and few-shot learning covers the case with more than one.

explainer.example: A system is shown one photo of a new product and must decide whether later photos show that same product.
